To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a family of highly substituted porphyin thioethes has been synthesized from 2.3.7,8, 12,13, 17,18-octethyl-5, 10, 15,20-tetrainitro-porphyrin (OETNP) by a SNAr mechanism.

the synthesis of a series of porphyrin thiols was achieved by nitro displacement on a single tetranitroporphin precursor and that X-ray analysis of the products revealed the conformational properties of these new meso-thio-substituted porphyins and the structural effects of an increased degree of nitro-substitution.
the synthesis and crystallographic characterization of highly substituted porphyin thioethors and nitroporphyrins were achieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a family of highly substituted porphyin thioethes via nitro displacement in H2OETN.
the synthesis of a new family of meso-substitution porphyrins and the structural characterization of these new molecules by single crystal X-ray analysis.
the synthesis, structural characterization and reactivity of highly substituted meso-nitroporphyrins, and the preparation of novel porphyrin derivatives from these nitro precursors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nitration of porphyrins is a useful synthetic method for the preparation of a large family of highly substituted porphinoids, and that these nitro compounds are useful precursors for the preparation of other porphyrinoids.
the porphyrin core is highly sensitive to the steric demands of the nitro group and that the nitro group is a powerful tool to induce a high degree of porphyrin distortion.
the nitro group in porphyrin is not a good leaving group, but rather it is a good electron withdrawing group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitro group can be used as a versatile functional group for the synthesis of highly substituted porphyinoids.
the porphyrin core is a highly versatile scaffold for the construction of a large variety of functionalized molecules.
we have synthesized a series of highly substituted meso-thioether porphyrins via SNAr reactions and have investigated the structural effects of nitro substitution on the porphyrin macrocycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis and study of highly substituted porphyinoids can lead to new insights into the effects of steric crowding on the conformational properties of porphyrins and related macrocycles.
nitro displacement reactions in porphyrins are a viable synthetic route for the synthesis of highly substituted porphyin derivatives.
the synthesis of highly substituted porphinoid macrocycles from simple nitro porphyrins is a rapid and convenient way of accessing new porphinoid compounds with interesting properties.
